claim: Separated two ways of ordering time: as past, present and future (which change) and as earlier and later (which never do). Argued the first is incoherent.

sources.label: McTaggart 1908, The Unreality of Time, Mind 17, 457

claim: Space by itself and time by itself fade into shadows; only a union of the two keeps an independent reality.
The past and present exist; the future does not yet. Reality grows as new slices are added to the top.

sources.label: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Time (the growing block)

claim: The objective world simply is, it does not happen. Only consciousness, crawling up the worldline of its body, lights one slice of it at a time.

sources.label: Weyl 1949, Philosophy of Mathematics and Natural Science (Princeton University Press)

claim: If what is simultaneous with something real is real, special relativity forces the future to be as real as the present.

sources.label: Rietdijk 1966, A Rigorous Proof of Determinism Derived from the Special Theory of Relativity, Philosophy of Science 33, 341

claim: Made the same argument independently: relativity leaves no room for a privileged present, so future events are already real.

sources.label: Putnam 1967, Time and Physical Geometry, Journal of Philosophy 64, 240

claim: Replied that the only frame-free notion of 'already happened' is an event's past light cone. Becoming can be relative to each event, without a block.

sources.label: Stein 1968, On Einstein–Minkowski Space–Time, Journal of Philosophy 65, 5

claim: Popularized the argument with two people walking past each other while a fleet sets off from Andromeda, or doesn't yet.

sources.label: The Rietdijk–Putnam argument and Penrose's Andromeda version

claim: Proposed an evolving, “crystallizing” block: quantum events settle the future as they happen, so the block grows.

sources.label: Ellis 2006, Physics in the Real Universe: Time and Spacetime (arXiv:gr-qc/0605049)
